To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the virulence of Sh. flexneri is dependent on the terminal glucose component in its polysaccharide antigen.
“the terminal glucose component of the O antigen plays a role as a virulence factor in tissue-growing capacity of S. flexneri var.Y.”

the virulence of S. flexneri Y is due to the presence of a phage and that the terminal glucose residue of O antigen, whether of natural or conversion origin, is a virulence factor for tissue-growing capacity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of lysogenic conversion in the pathogenesis of S. flexneri.

the role of the terminal glucose component as a virulence factor of the Shigella flexncri group, and with the role of other antigens, especially those of lysogenic conversion origin, in the virulence of this group.
the role in virulence of the antigens derived from lysogenic conversion of S. flexneri.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the virulence of the parent strain is not due to the presence of phage, but to the presence of the terminal glucose residue of the O antigen.
, in S. flexneri, the virulence factors are not confined to the O antigen and the phage.
the virulence factors of Sh. flexneri are composed of the O antigen and its terminal glucose residue and that the phage is an auxiliary agent in the tissue-growing capacity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the lysogenic conversion of S. flexneri var Y (NTCC4839) by phage 7, 10 and by phage 8, 9 resulted in the loss of virulence to the mouse and to the guinea-pig eye, but an increase of the tissue-growing ability for chicken embryos.

the lysogenic convertants of Sh. flexneri var Y, which were derived from the parent strain by means of the bacteriophages, lost the virulence to the mouse and the guinea pig, but regained an increased tissue-growing ability for the chicken embryos.
the virulence of S. flexneri Y was due to the combined effect of the defective tissue-growing capacity of the parent strain and the loss of virulence factors in the lysogenic convertants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the virulence of Sh. flexneri is not only determined by the presence of the virulence plasmid, but is also dependent on the antigenic composition of the O antigen.
Shigella virulence is not only a property of the bacterium but is a complex interaction with the host and its environment.
Shigella flexnieri is an important pathogen that causes diarrhea and dysentery in humans and animals.
